Partner
pärt´ner
n. (one who shares in a work; rendering Greek koinonos and metochos)
From part. A partner shares both the labour and the take — and the Gospels use the word of a fishing business that became something else.

Biblical Definition

A partner shares in a work. James and John are named as “partners with Simon” in the fishing trade, and their boats sink together under the catch (Luk 5:7,10). Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus with a striking phrase: “If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself” (Phm 17), and warns against being partakers with idolaters at their table (1Co 10:20).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines partner as one who partakes or shares with another; a sharer; and an associate in business, one who has a joint interest.

expand to see more

PARTNER, n. One who partakes or shares with another; a partaker; an associate.

2. An associate in any business or occupation; a joint owner of stock or capital.

3. One who dances with another.

Key Scripture

Luk 5:10 — "And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men."

Phm 17 — "If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself."

Luk 5:7 — "And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink."

1Co 10:20 — "But I say, that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils."

Modern Corruption

Partnership in the gospel is described in financial language and rarely in personal ones, and Paul stakes his own standing on a runaway slave being received as himself.

expand to see more

Philemon 17 is one of the boldest sentences Paul wrote: if thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself. Onesimus had run away and was legally at his master's mercy; Paul does not argue slavery in the abstract but interposes his own account — if he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account. Partnership here is not a funding relationship but a willingness to be treated as the offender.

Luke 5 shows partnership becoming something else. James and John were partners with Simon in a business, and after a catch that broke the nets and sank the boats, Christ said, from henceforth thou shalt catch men. They forsook all and followed him. The commercial partnership was real, profitable, and abandoned on the day it succeeded most spectacularly.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek koinonos (G2844), a sharer, partner — the root of fellowship; metochos (G3353), a partaker, in Luke 5:7.

expand to see more

Greek koinonos (G2844) — partner, sharer; Luke 5:10, Philemon 17, 1 Corinthians 10:20, 2 Peter 1:4.

Greek metochos (G3353) — partaker, partner; Luke 5:7, Hebrews 3:1, 14.

Greek koinonia (G2842) — fellowship; the abstract of the same root.

Usage

"“If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself” — standing staked on another man."

"“Which were partners with Simon” — a business abandoned at its best moment."

"“Put that on mine account” — partnership as assumed liability."
